Variants.Content: House Selmy is rooted in Harvest Hall in the Stormlands, and its sigil is connected to wheat ears, farmland, and knightly traditions. The house is best known as Barristan Selmy, but the glory of the White Knights should not overwhelm the house itself: there are still fields, tenants, horses, marriage alliances, and feudal duties in Harvest Hall. Selmy was not of the most illustrious origins, but he was able to maintain his position among the Stormlands nobility through combat, service, and discreet marriage. If a family bets all its honor on a single legend, the hall will feel particularly empty after the legend leaves.

The nobles of the Stormlands both admired and sobered Selmy: Barristan allowed the family name to spread throughout the Seven Kingdoms, but it also made it easy for others to forget that the Harvest Hall needed ordinary lords to run it. The white robe belongs to one person, and the family's lands and debts belong to each generation.

Harvest Hall farmers know that the wheat ears ripen earlier than the Knight's Ballad. Soldiers were proud of the name Barristan, and farmers looked to see if their lords protected the harvests, repaired the roads, and didn't send all the good horses away. Legend can illuminate the door of a house, but cannot pay the food tax for it.
